newsitem.title: USA: GM's Delphi to stop output at N.J. plant.
newsitem.headline: GM's Delphi to stop output at N.J. plant.

text.p: Delphi Interior & Lighting Systems said Monday it will cease production at its Trenton plant, located in Ewing, N.J., during the 1998 calendar year.
Delphi Interior is a division of General Motors Corp's Delphi Automotive Systems unit.
Approximately 900 employees work at Trenton in the two shift operation that produces automotive moldings, powder painted exterior products and power seat adjusters.
The decision to close the plant came after efforts over several years to return it to profitability and increase its competitiveness.
Between now and the time production ends many of the plant's products will no longer be in production due to phase out of current models, Delphi said.
The assembly of power seat adjusters will be consolidated at Delphi Interior & Lighting's Grand Rapids, Mich., facility.
Delphi said it will continue to work closely with the United Auto Workers union, salaried employees, the local community and the State of New Jersey to manage the transition.
